mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate reduces the cost of capital for corporations, increasing present value of future cash flows and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the CPI index exceeds 301.0, it signals persistent inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates, which compresses equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns within 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite CPIAUCSL > 301.0.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts and retail sales indicates robust consumer demand, boosting corporate earnings and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When both HOUST and RSAFS increase by > 0.5% in the prior month, S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in > 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In low unemployment regimes (UNRATE < 3.5%), tight labor markets fuel wage inflation, leading the Federal Reserve to tighten policy and cause negative S&P 500 returns within 20 days.
failure_condition: In periods where UNRATE < 3.5%, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Higher industrial production reflects a strong economy, supporting corporate profits and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO increases by > 0.5% month-over-month, 60-day forward returns are negative in > 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A quarterly GDP growth rate below 2.0% signals economic weakness, reducing corporate earnings expectations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: When GDPC1 growth rate < 2.0%, 60-day forward returns are positive in > 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent increases in the federal funds rate and CPI indicate an active monetary tightening cycle, which raises discount rates and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns within 20 days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL rises by > 0.2% in the prior month, S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in > 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In high employment growth regimes (PAYEMS growth > 200k), strong labor market conditions support consumer spending and corporate revenue growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where PAYEMS growth > 200k, 5-day forward returns are negative in > 50% of cases.
